import pandas as pd

def main():
    # Source file paths
    source_files = [
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_30/test_0.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_30/test_1.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_30/test_2.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_30/test_3.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_30/test_4.csv"
    ]

    # Read all source CSV files into a list of DataFrames
    # index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column as per Hint 24
    dfs = [pd.read_csv(f, index_col=0) for f in source_files]

    # All source tables have exactly the same schema as the target table
    # According to Hint 2 and Hint 4, we should UNION all source tables
    # because schemas are identical and target schema matches source schema

    # Concatenate all DataFrames (union)
    combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

    # Ensure columns are in the exact order as target schema
    target_columns = [
        'categories', 'commentCount', 'completed', 'copyright', 'cover', 'cover_timestamp',
        'createDate', 'deleted', 'description', 'firstPartId', 'firstPublishedPart.createDate',
        'firstPublishedPart.id', 'id', 'language.id', 'language.name', 'lastPublishedPart.createDate',
        'lastPublishedPart.id', 'length', 'mature', 'modifyDate', 'numParts', 'parts', 'rating',
        'readCount', 'tags', 'title', 'url', 'user.avatar', 'user.fullname', 'user.name', 'voteCount'
    ]

    # Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
    combined_df = combined_df[target_columns]

    # Data type enforcement based on target schema:
    # categories: string (can be list or string, keep as is)
    # commentCount: integer
    # completed: boolean
    # copyright: integer
    # cover: string
    # cover_timestamp: string (ISO datetime string)
    # createDate: string (ISO datetime string)
    # deleted: boolean
    # description: string (may contain NaN)
    # firstPartId: integer
    # firstPublishedPart.createDate: string
    # firstPublishedPart.id: integer
    # id: integer
    # language.id: integer
    # language.name: string
    # lastPublishedPart.createDate: string
    # lastPublishedPart.id: integer
    # length: integer
    # mature: boolean
    # modifyDate: string
    # numParts: integer
    # parts: string (JSON-like string)
    # rating: integer
    # readCount: integer
    # tags: string (JSON-like string)
    # title: string
    # url: string
    # user.avatar: string
    # user.fullname: string (may contain NaN)
    # user.name: string
    # voteCount: integer

    # Convert columns to appropriate types carefully

    # Integer columns
    int_cols = [
        'commentCount', 'copyright', 'firstPartId', 'firstPublishedPart.id', 'id',
        'language.id', 'lastPublishedPart.id', 'length', 'numParts', 'rating',
        'readCount', 'voteCount'
    ]
    for col in int_cols:
        combined_df[col] = pd.to_numeric(combined_df[col], errors='coerce').fillna(0).astype(int)

    # Boolean columns
    bool_cols = ['completed', 'deleted', 'mature']
    for col in bool_cols:
        # Some source data might have True/False or 1/0, convert accordingly
        combined_df[col] = combined_df[col].astype(bool)

    # String columns (including JSON-like strings and datetime strings)
    str_cols = [
        'categories', 'cover', 'cover_timestamp', 'createDate', 'description',
        'firstPublishedPart.createDate', 'language.name', 'lastPublishedPart.createDate',
        'modifyDate', 'parts', 'tags', 'title', 'url', 'user.avatar', 'user.fullname', 'user.name'
    ]
    for col in str_cols:
        # Convert to string, keep NaN as is (except for user.fullname which can be NaN)
        combined_df[col] = combined_df[col].astype('object').where(combined_df[col].notnull(), None)

    # Save the combined DataFrame to the target CSV file
    output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_30/target_multisource_cot.csv"
    combined_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
